findings.title: KeyError/TypeError on integrations whose metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. Integrations created through paths that don't set the sender metadata (e.g. created by the pipeline itself via build_integration, where `state.get("sender")` may be absent, or older integrations installed before sender tracking) have no `sender` key in metadata, so this raises KeyError (or TypeError if sender is not a dict), producing a 500 error page instead of the intended error response. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat missing sender explicitly.

findings.title: User verification is skipped when the Integration does not exist yet
findings.body: The authenticated-user-vs-installer check only executes in the branch where the Integration already exists but has no OrganizationIntegration (line 500-505). If the Integration.DoesNotExist branch is taken (line 481-482) — e.g. the installation webhook hasn't been processed yet, or the integration was deleted — the pipeline proceeds with `pipeline.next_step()` without any verification that the currently authenticated GitHub user is the one who installed the app, and the integration is then built with unverified state. This is a race/bypass of the very control this PR adds; the check (or a sender-present requirement) should also apply on the fresh-install path.

findings.title: get_user_info / token exchange failures raise unhandled exceptions
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (and the `safe_urlopen` call at line 423) are not wrapped in error handling. If GitHub's /user endpoint returns an error, rate limits, or the HTTP layer raises (timeout/connection error), the exception propagates and the user gets a 500 instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." error page. The code only guards against a missing `login` key, not against the call failing.

findings.title: installation_id may be None in the direct-from-GitHub redirect
findings.body: When a request arrives with `setup_action=install` and no pipeline, `request.GET.get("installation_id")` can be None (GitHub can send other setup_action values or the parameter may be stripped), and `reverse("integration-installation", args=[provider_id, None])` will render a URL like `.../github/None`, sending the user to a broken page. Guard for a missing installation_id and fall through to the "Invalid request." handling.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 installation path
findings.body: The rewritten test asserts on "Invalid installation request." but the second request uses a hardcoded state (`ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`) that does not match the pipeline signature, so the response comes from the state-mismatch branch, not from `get_installation_info` returning 404 ("The GitHub installation could not be found." path in build_integration). The original scenario — a valid OAuth flow where the installation lookup 404s — is no longer covered; add a test that drives the flow with a valid signature and a 404 stubbed installation endpoint.

findings.title: Disabled (non-ACTIVE) integrations produce a misleading generic error
findings.body: In the 'Integration exists without OrganizationIntegration' branch, `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` fails for integrations whose status is DISABLED/PENDING_DELETION but whose OrganizationIntegration was already removed, yielding the generic "Invalid installation request." error instead of the pending-deletion message, and preventing reinstallation of a legitimately removable integration. The pending-deletion check above only inspects OrganizationIntegration rows, so a deactivated integration row with no OI rows hits this path.
